newsitem.title: USA: N.J. approves Orange, Pemberton school spending.
newsitem.headline: N.J. approves Orange, Pemberton school spending.

text.p: New Jersey on Monday approved plans by school districts in Orange and Pemberton to spend additional state aid.
The state's Department of Education said Orange would receive $6.3 million in additional state aid for fiscal 1998 and Pemberton would get $5.7 million.

The two districts are among 28 so-called "special needs" districts set apart by court rulings that struck down the state's system of public school financing. The courts ruled the districts should be given more aid to compensate for disparities between rich and poor districts.
The 28 districts are set to receive a total of $246 million in court-ordered aid increases, but each must first win approval from the state on how the money would be spent.
